symptom: An integration expects a documented borrower-status redemption-fee waiver, but deployed-source simulation applies the governed fee path without that branch.
prerequisites: The integration used borrower status or descriptive prose to remove the fee rather than the active call path.
diagnosticSteps: Resolve the active BorrowerOperations and TroveManager deployments and version-matched source.
Read the governed redemption input at one block and evaluate the canonical actual-fill fee model.
Simulate the exact redemption and reconcile actual fill and fee events rather than assuming the attempted amount.
expected: The documentation-derived waiver removes the fee for the described account status.
observed: The pinned deployed call path contains no such account-status branch; the discrepancy is resolved by the redemption canonical owner.
control: Independent mainnet and testnet fixed-block reads reported the governed input, and source inspection covers fee calculation and settlement.
verifiedCause: The waiver prose is stale for the recorded deployments. This record does not infer intended future policy.
safeMitigation: Use active deployment/source evidence, current governed reads, canonical actual-fill math, exact-call simulation, and event/post-state reconciliation. Do not hard-code a waiver from account labels or docs.
limitations: Governed inputs and deployments are volatile and must be reread/resolved.
The redemption entrypoint has no minimum-received argument; fee diagnosis does not replace fill reconciliation.
